title: The Visual Pathway: From Retina to Striate Cortex & Dual Processing Streams
description: Examine photoreceptors, the retinogeniculate pathway, Hubel & Wiesel's cortical columns, and the dorsal ('where/how') vs. ventral ('what') streams.

slides.title: Photoreceptors: Rods vs. Cones 👁️
slides.content:
# The Duplicity Theory of Vision

The human retina contains two fundamentally different classes of photoreceptors:

| Feature | Rods | Cones |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Quantity** | ~120 million per retina | ~6 million per retina |
| **Retinal Distribution** | Dense in periphery; entirely absent from central fovea | Concentrated heavily in the **fovea centralis** |
| **Light Sensitivity** | Extremely high; specialized for dim light (**Scotopic vision**) | Lower sensitivity; specialized for daylight (**Photopic vision**) |
| **Acuity & Resolution** | Low acuity (hundreds of rods converge on one ganglion cell) | High acuity (1:1 cone-to-ganglion cell wiring in fovea) |
| **Color Vision** | Achromatic (single photopigment: rhodopsin) | **Trichromatic** (3 photopigments: S-blue, M-green, L-red) |

slides.title: The Retinogeniculate Pathway & V1 📐
slides.content:
## From Retina to Striate Cortex

1. Photoreceptors synapse on **bipolar cells**, which synapse on **retinal ganglion cells (RGCs)**.
2. RGC axons form the **optic nerve** (CN II), exiting through the optic disc (creating our physiological **blind spot**).
3. At the **optic chiasm**, axons from the nasal hemiretinas decussate (cross the midline), while temporal hemiretinas stay ipsilateral.
4. Optic tracts project to the **Lateral Geniculate Nucleus (LGN)** of the thalamus (Layers 1-2: Magnocellular / motion; Layers 3-6: Parvocellular / color and fine detail).
5. Optic radiations carry signals to **Primary Visual Cortex (V1 / Striate Cortex)**.

*Hubel & Wiesel's Discovery*: V1 neurons do not respond to round spots of light; they respond to **oriented bars and edges**:
* **Simple Cells**: Sensitive to bar orientation in a specific retinal position.
* **Complex Cells**: Sensitive to orientation and directional movement anywhere in the receptive field.

quizData.question: Which LGN layers receive inputs from magnocellular retinal ganglion cells specialized for detecting movement and broad outlines?
quizData.explanation: Layers 1 and 2 of the LGN are the magnocellular layers, specialized for high temporal resolution, flicker, and motion perception.

slides.title: The Dual Streams: What vs. Where Pathways 🛤️
slides.content:
## Two Visual Processing Streams (Ungerleider & Mishkin)

Upon leaving primary visual cortex, visual information splits into two anatomically and functionally distinct processing streams:

### 1. The Dorsal Stream ('Where / How' Pathway):
* **Route**: V1 $\rightarrow$ V2 $\rightarrow$ V5/MT $\rightarrow$ **Posterior Parietal Cortex**.
* **Function**: Computes spatial relationships, motion detection, and visually guided motor action (reaching and grasping).
* **Lesion Pathology**: **Akinetopsia** (motion blindness—seeing movement as frozen snapshots) and **Optic Ataxia** (inability to guide reaching toward objects despite seeing them).

### 2. The Ventral Stream ('What' Pathway):
* **Route**: V1 $\rightarrow$ V2 $\rightarrow$ V4 $\rightarrow$ **Inferior Temporal Cortex**.
* **Function**: Object recognition, high-resolution shape analysis, color perception (V4), and facial identification (FFA).
* **Lesion Pathology**: **Visual Object Agnosia** (inability to recognize objects by sight) and **Prosopagnosia** (face blindness).

quizData.question: Patient D.F. suffered carbon monoxide poisoning damaging her ventral stream. She cannot identify a slot's orientation, but can effortlessly slip a card into it. Why?

options.text: Her intact dorsal 'how/action' stream guides motor reaching despite ventral stream object recognition failure
She has exceptional color vision in her fovea
Her auditory system compensates by echoing
Her corpus callosum was severed during surgery

quizData.explanation: Milner & Goodale demonstrated that D.F.'s dorsal stream ('vision-for-action') remained intact, allowing accurate motor action despite ventral stream agnosia.
